cases.notes: max_frame_payload = 32768 needs the 4-byte varint62 80 00 80 00 inside TLV type 7, length 4 (WIRE_EXAMPLES 1.26)

preface_padding (setting 12) carries ignored bytes ff c0 ff that are not a valid varint62, and every setting keeps its default; settings_len counts the padding TLV, so re-encoding the parsed preface without padding does not reproduce these bytes (WIRE_EXAMPLES 1.28)

preface_padding (setting 12) with an empty value is valid and ignored, and every setting keeps its default; settings_len counts the 2-byte padding TLV, so re-encoding the parsed preface without padding does not reproduce these bytes (WIRE_EXAMPLES 1.28a)
the duplicated singleton stream_priority drops the whole metadata block while the DATA still opens stream 4 with payload "hi" (WIRE_EXAMPLES 1.20)
the second stream_priority TLV duplicates the first, so the block is dropped before its non-canonical value 40 02 is interpreted; the DATA still opens stream 4 with payload "hi" (SPEC 7.2)
the duplicated singleton debug_text drops only the DIAG block; ABORT(REFUSED_STREAM) keeps its primary semantics (WIRE_EXAMPLES 1.22a)

DIAG-TLV retry_after_millis = 1 encoded non-canonically as 40 01 is ignored as semantically invalid diagnostic metadata; ABORT(REFUSED_STREAM) keeps its primary semantics (SPEC 3.2, 7.1; WIRE_EXAMPLES 1.22b)
ext_type 99 is unassigned; receivers ignore it without failing the session (WIRE_EXAMPLES 1.27)
padded PING whose bytes 8..15 are ping_padding_tag(0x0123456789abcdef, token) (SPEC 6.4, WIRE_EXAMPLES 1.29)
DATA("hi") with frame_length = 5 whose stream_id = 4 is encoded non-canonically as 40 04 in the frame header (SPEC 3.2)

first byte announces a 4-byte varint62 but only 3 bytes are present; PROTOCOL applies to frame-header and preface integers (SPEC 3.2), while a truncated mandatory payload field is FRAME_SIZE (see invalid_truncated_mandatory_payload_varint)
frame_length = 16387, code = DATA, stream_id = 4, derived payload length = 16385
frame_length = 1 leaves no room for stream_id (SPEC 4.3)
frame_length = 2 but stream_id = 16384 announces a 4-byte encoding; frame_length < 1 + encoded_length(stream_id) (SPEC 4.3)
MAX_DATA on stream 0 with max_offset = 1 encoded non-canonically as 40 01; malformed mandatory payload field (SPEC 3.2, 4.3)
MAX_DATA on stream 0 whose max_offset announces 2 bytes but the payload ends after 1 (SPEC 3.2, 4.3)
STOP_SENDING on stream 4 with an empty payload; mandatory error_code missing (SPEC 4.3)
MAX_DATA on stream 0 with canonical max_offset = 5 followed by one trailing byte (SPEC 4.3)
PONG on stream 0 with a 7-byte payload (SPEC 4.3, 6.5)
EXT on stream 0 with an empty payload; derived_payload_length < encoded_length(ext_type) is the frame-specific PROTOCOL exception (SPEC 6.11)

cases.description: A preface settings block repeats the same setting ID.
A peer advertises an unsupported role value.
Both peers use role=auto with the same tie_breaker_nonce.
A peer uses role=auto with tie_breaker_nonce = 0.
A peer advertises max_frame_payload below the v1 minimum.
A peer advertises max_control_payload_bytes below the v1 minimum.
A peer advertises max_extension_payload_bytes below the v1 minimum.
A peer preface does not start with the ASCII magic ZMUX.
A peer preface uses an unsupported preface_ver = 2.
The local and peer [min_proto, max_proto] ranges do not overlap.
Both peers explicitly request the same role (initiator/initiator; responder/responder is symmetric).
A peer preface advertises settings_len = 4097; the receiver rejects it from the length field before reading the settings bytes.
A preface settings block repeats preface_padding (setting 12).
A preface settings block repeats an unknown setting ID (63).
A known varint setting (max_frame_payload) has an empty TLV value.
A known varint setting value 80 00 announces a 4-byte varint62 but its TLV holds 2 bytes (the old WIRE_EXAMPLES 1.26 mistake).
A known varint setting carries max_frame_payload = 16384 in a non-canonical 8-byte varint62.
A known varint setting value is followed by a trailing byte inside its TLV.
A settings TLV length overruns settings_tlv.
A frame advertises frame_length smaller than the mandatory code plus shortest stream_id encoding.
EXT derives a payload shorter than the encoded ext_type prefix.
A frame_length remains too small for the actual encoded stream_id prefix after stream_id parsing.
PING carries a forbidden non-zero flag.
PONG payload is shorter than the required 8-byte token.
A locally originated PING chooses a payload longer than the smaller of local and peer control-payload limits.
ABORT is invalid on the session control stream_id 0.
MAX_DATA carries trailing bytes beyond its one canonical max_offset field.
BLOCKED carries trailing bytes beyond its one canonical blocked_at field.
A frame uses an unassigned core frame type.
PRIORITY_UPDATE repeats a singleton STREAM-METADATA-TLV.
PRIORITY_UPDATE contains a structurally truncated TLV header.
PRIORITY_UPDATE contains a TLV value length that overruns the enclosing payload.
PRIORITY_UPDATE on an open stream carries stream_priority = 2 encoded non-canonically as 40 02; the malformed standardized value makes the EXT payload malformed.
PRIORITY_UPDATE arrives without negotiated priority_update capability.
PRIORITY_UPDATE targets a previously unused valid stream ID.
PRIORITY_UPDATE targets a stream that is already terminal.
An unknown EXT subtype is received.
A DATA frame uses OPEN_METADATA without negotiated open_metadata capability.
A DATA frame uses OPEN_METADATA after the stream is already open.
OPEN_METADATA repeats a singleton STREAM-METADATA-TLV on the opening DATA frame.
Incoming DATA would exceed the effective stream MAX_DATA limit.
A stream-scoped MAX_DATA arrives for a previously unused valid stream ID.
A stream-scoped BLOCKED arrives for a previously unused valid stream ID.
A STOP_SENDING arrives for a previously unused valid stream ID.
A RESET arrives for a previously unused valid stream ID.
Incoming DATA would exceed the effective session MAX_DATA limit.
A peer opens a new stream ID that skips lower still-unused IDs of the same class.
BLOCKED arrives from the non-sending side of a unidirectional stream.
DATA arrives from the non-sending side of an opened unidirectional stream.
MAX_DATA arrives from the sending side of a unidirectional stream.
STOP_SENDING arrives from the sending side of a unidirectional stream.
RESET arrives from the non-sending side of a unidirectional stream.
A later GOAWAY increases one of its per-stream-class acceptance watermarks.
A provisional local open is cancelled before first-frame commit but still advances the next local stream_id cursor.
Hidden control-opened-only nonterminal state exceeds the local hard cap but the implementation neither sheds nor refuses the newest hidden stream.

Many stopped directions together exceed the repository-default aggregate late-data allowance while the implementation keeps buffering late tail bytes instead of discarding them with session budget release.
A peer repeatedly opens and immediately aborts streams at abusive rates while the implementation applies no churn limit or disconnect policy.
